```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Convert charges to costs

Charges are not costs. `nis_cost()` estimates hospital costs by multiplying
charges by `CCR_NIS`, then expresses both cost and charges in a selected
reference-year dollar using annual CPI-U indices.

```{r cost}
charges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS) |>
  dplyr::collect()
adjusted <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2024)
head(adjusted[c("YEAR", "TOTCHG", "cost_adj", "charges_adj")])
```

`cost_adj` contains the estimated cost in 2024 dollars and `charges_adj`
contains adjusted charges. These are synthetic amounts intended only to show
the calculation.

## Check provenance

The direct result records the source fields, price index, base year,
multipliers, and invalid input counts.

```{r provenance}
nis_cost_provenance(adjusted)
```

Missing or non-positive CCR values produce missing costs; the corresponding
adjusted charge can still be present. Describe the CCR and inflation choices
when reporting results.

`nis_design(..., dollars = 2024)` can add these adjusted values to the survey
design when `CCR_NIS` and the selected charge column are kept.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Calling inflation-adjusted charges “costs” without applying a CCR.
> - Treating missing or invalid CCR values as zero cost.
> - Combining `TOTCHG_2023` silently with earlier `TOTCHG`; its definition is
>   different and the package documents the 2023 layout as unverified.
> - Dropping provenance attributes through later data-frame operations before
>   recording the adjustment method.

See [`nis_cost()`](../reference/nis_cost.html),
[`nis_cost_provenance()`](../reference/nis_cost_provenance.html), and
[`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html).
